title: Heavy-Hole--Light-Hole Mixing and Spin--Photon Coupling in Germanium Flopping-Mode Qubits
abstract: Intrinsic spin--orbit interaction in germanium provides electrically active flopping-mode qubits without requiring magnetic-field gradients to generate spin--charge hybridization. We study double quantum dots (DQDs) with a multiband Luttinger--Kohn framework that retains heavy-hole (HH) and light-hole (LH) states on equal footing. Modeling vertical confinement with a finite confinement potential along the growth direction brings selected subbands into a regime of appreciable HH--LH mixing. This admixture activates electric-dipole spin-coupling through LH--LH and LH--HH transitions, complementing the conventional HH--HH pseudospin-flip resonance. For the parameter sets considered, these additional channels can produce larger spin--photon figures of merit than the HH--HH transition. HH--LH mixing thus supplies a tunable ingredient for qubit--cavity coupling in germanium hole-spin qubits and extends the operating regimes available to circuit-QED architectures.
summary: This theoretical study models hole-spin qubits in Germanium quantum dots, focusing on the role of Heavy-Hole/Light-Hole mixing. By incorporating this mixing, the authors show that new electric-dipole coupling channels become active, potentially leading to stronger coupling to microwave cavities than previously expected. This provides a key, tunable mechanism for advancing circuit-QED quantum computing platforms.
main_problem: The study investigates how Heavy-Hole (HH)–Light-Hole (LH) mixing affects the spin–photon coupling mechanism in Germanium (Ge) flopping-mode qubits.
main_result: The HH–LH mixing activates additional electric-dipole spin-coupling channels (LH–LH and LH–HH) that can yield larger spin–photon figures of merit compared to the conventional HH–HH transition.
method: The authors use a multiband Luttinger–Kohn framework within a Double Quantum Dot (DQD) model, analyzing the Hamiltonian structure and coupling to a cavity using input–output theory.
model_or_system: The system is a DQD in a Ge/SiGe heterostructure, modeled using a Hamiltonian incorporating kinetic, confinement, and spin-orbit interaction terms. The analysis focuses on the $J=3/2$ valence band subspace, treating HH and LH states explicitly.
key_observables: Spin–photon coupling strength, spin–photon figure of merit, and linewidth for various spin-flip transitions (HH–HH, LH–LH, LH–HH).
important_parameters: Confinement depths ($U_{HH}, U_{LH}$), interdot tunneling amplitudes ($t$), and the strength of the spin-orbit coupling ($\alpha_R$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the applicability of the effective-mass approximation and simplifies the orbital sector by restricting the in-plane basis to the ground state ($j=l=0$).
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the Ge DQD structure, detailing the confinement potential and the various tunneling processes (HH–HH, LH–LH, LH–HH) involved in spin-photon coupling.
paper_structure: The paper builds the model by defining the full Hamiltonian using the Luttinger–Kohn framework, incorporating vertical confinement via a finite potential well. It then analyzes the resulting Hamiltonian in the DQD basis, demonstrating how HH–LH mixing introduces new, potentially superior, coupling channels for qubit-cavity interaction.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the engineering of quantum coupling mechanisms in solid-state qubits, which is central to scalable quantum computing architectures. The explicit inclusion of valence band mixing provides a tunable knob for enhancing qubit-photon interaction.

The left panel shows a narrow magnetic-field window around the low-field resonance, where the cavity response ex- hibits an avoided crossing associated with the hybridization between the cavity mode and the spin-like transition. The right panel shows the response at the intermediate-field reso- nance, where the charge character dominates and the vacuum Rabi splitting is no longer visible because of strong charge de- coherence.

The black dashed lines indicate the boundaries of a 1% tolerance window around the resonance condition. The C-shaped resonance has a predominantly charge-like character, and therefore no vac- uum Rabi splitting is observed. We chose ωc/2π = 6.54 GHz.

Spintronics.note: The new paper directly models spin-photon coupling in a semiconductor quantum dot system using a Hamiltonian approach, which is highly relevant to the cavity QED aspects of spintronics.
